items.prompt: We ___ a lovely film at the cinema last night.

explanation.en: See is irregular. The past simple form is saw.

optionNotes.en: Correct: saw is the past simple of see.
Seen is the participle and needs have in front of it.
See is the base form; last night needs the past.

items.prompt: I ___ my keys this morning, so I was late for work.

explanation.en: Lose is irregular and its past form is lost.

optionNotes.en: Correct: lost is the past simple.
Losing needs a form of be before it, and this morning is finished.
optionNotes.es: Losing necesita be delante, y la mañana ya ha terminado.

optionNotes.en: Lose is the base form, but this morning is finished.

items.prompt: He ___ English at university for three years before moving abroad.

explanation.en: After a consonant, y changes to i before -ed.
explanation.es: Consonante + y: study pasa a studied.

optionNotes.en: Study is the base form, but he moved abroad in the past.
optionNotes.es: Study es la forma base, pero se fue al extranjero en el pasado.

optionNotes.en: Studies is present, but the story is in the past.
optionNotes.es: Studies es presente, pero la historia es pasada.

items.prompt: A: Did you enjoy the concert? B: Yes, we ___ a great time.

explanation.en: Have is irregular. Its past form is had.

optionNotes.en: Correct: had is the past simple of have.
Having needs a form of be before it: we were having a great time.
optionNotes.es: Having necesita be delante: we were having a great time.

optionNotes.en: Have is present, but the concert has finished.

items.prompt: He didn't ___ the email until Monday, so the client was angry.

explanation.en: After didn't the verb is in the base form.

optionNotes.en: Sent is already past, so it is not used after didn't.
Sends is a present form with -s.

items.prompt: What time ___ you get home last night? I called you at eleven.

explanation.en: A question about a finished action in the past uses did + base verb.

optionNotes.en: Do is present, but last night is past.
Were cannot be followed by the base verb get.
